German Morning Routine Verbs: A1 Vocabulary Practice

Practise aufstehen, duschen, frühstücken and losgehen in a German morning routine. Study verb meanings, translations and explained A1 answers.

A1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Vocabulary and usage

Aufstehen means to get up, duschen to shower, frühstücken to eat breakfast and losgehen to set off. Aufstehen and losgehen are separable: Ich stehe auf; ich gehe los. After a modal verb such as möchte, the complete infinitive stays together at the end.

Common mistake to avoid

Frühstücken already means to have breakfast. Do not translate have breakfast word for word using haben plus frühstücken.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Notice each word’s meaning, article and common word partners in context.

Worked example 1Am Sonntag stehe ich um neun auf.On Sunday I get up at nine.
Worked example 2Danach dusche ich kurz.After that I take a quick shower.
Worked example 3Wir frühstücken gemeinsam am Fenster.We have breakfast together by the window.
Worked example 4Um halb acht gehe ich los.I set off at half past seven.

Practice: choose the matching word

Choose the word from the bank that matches the English cue and sentence. Use each item once; keep its spelling and capitalisation. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Word bank: aufstehen · duschen · frühstücken · losgehen

Question 1. Morgen möchte ich um sechs ___. (get up)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: aufstehen

After möchte, the separable verb remains the infinitive aufstehen.

Question 2. Nach dem Sport möchte ich ___. (shower)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: duschen

Duschen means to take a shower.

Question 3. Vor der Schule möchte ich in Ruhe ___. (have breakfast)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: frühstücken

Frühstücken expresses eating breakfast as one verb.

Question 4. Wir müssen jetzt ___. (set off)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: losgehen

Losgehen means to leave or set off; müssen takes the infinitive.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
